S-PRO-1.text: The Artemis Lunar Lander touches down on grey lunar regolith. Dust settles.

S-PRO-1.speaker: MILO
S-PRO-1.text: Touchdown confirmed on Shackleton Crater Rim! First Light Outpost systems online.

S-PRO-1.speaker: Leo
S-PRO-1.text: Welcome to the Moon, Commander! Shackleton Rim is one of the harshest places in the solar system. Our survival depends entirely on the machines working around us.

S-PRO-1.speaker: MILO
S-PRO-1.text: All telemetry channels are streaming. Let us tour each base sector so you understand how every machine keeps our crew alive.

S-BASE-TOUR.text: Holographic telemetry highlights the glowing First Light Outpost complex.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: MILO
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Welcome to First Light Outpost, Commander! You are looking at a complete, self-sustaining lunar survival base on Shackleton Crater Rim.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Leo
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Our lives depend on every machine here working together in balance. Without them, the vacuum and radiation are fatal. Let's inspect each sector so you understand how they keep us alive.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Amir
S-BASE-TOUR.text: First up: ENERGY! Look at our 8 Solar Panels along the sunlit ridge. They convert sunlight into 160 kW of clean electrical power. But lunar dust settles on them constantly—so we must clean them regularly to keep power flowing!

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Amir
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Right beside them are 8 Battery Banks storing 800 kWh of energy. When the 12-hour lunar night falls, solar power drops to zero. Our batteries release stored power to keep the base alive until sunrise.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Amir
S-BASE-TOUR.text: And linking everything are our Power Cables—the heavy-duty electrical grid routing wattage between every generator, battery, and life-support machine.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Daniel
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Next: ATMOSPHERE & BREATHING. The four of us exhale toxic carbon dioxide with every breath. Without our 2 CO₂ Scrubbers, CO₂ would poison our blood within hours. They filter out 4 kg of toxic gas every single hour.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Nia
S-BASE-TOUR.text: And for fresh air, meet our Oxygen Electrolyzer! It splits liquid water (H₂O) into hydrogen and breathable oxygen, generating +2.5 kg of pure oxygen per hour.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Nia
S-BASE-TOUR.text: To supply water for breathing and drinking, our Water Recycling System purifies wastewater and humidity, reclaiming +3 liters of clean water every hour.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Daniel
S-BASE-TOUR.text: And if our primary loop ever drops below safe levels, the Emergency Oxygen Generator acts as our backup lifeline to immediately pressurize the cabin.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Amir
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Don't forget the extreme cold! Outside in shadow it drops to -180°C. Our automated Heating System pumps warmth through the core, maintaining cabin temperature safely at 21°C.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Nia
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Over in the Green Dome is our Growth Farm. Plants recycle carbon dioxide, produce supplemental oxygen, and grow fresh food to keep crew morale high and hunger away.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Leo
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Up top is our Lunar Soil Radiation Shield—a thick blanket of regolith blocking deadly cosmic rays. And if an X-class solar flare strikes, we evacuate to the Subterranean Storm Vault!

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: Leo
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Finally, our Earth Connection Channel keeps high-gain communication streaming to Houston, allowing emergency cargo resupplies when resources run thin.

S-BASE-TOUR.speaker: MILO
S-BASE-TOUR.text: Systems briefing complete. The outpost is yours to command! You can continue managing this pre-built base, or select 'Start building my own base' to design your own from scratch.

S-C1-1.speaker: Amir
S-C1-1.text: Power lines connected! 40 kilowatts of solar energy are pouring into the main breaker!

S-C1-1.speaker: Leo
S-C1-1.text: Outstanding work, Commander! With the power grid online, the habitat lights are on and our systems are fully operational.

S-C1-1.speaker: MILO
S-C1-1.text: Base telemetry unlocked. All life-support, oxygen, and resource monitoring channels are now active.

S-C1-2.text: A shrill alarm echoes through the habitat.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: CRITICAL ALERT: Primary compressed oxygen tank pressure dropping to zero! Valve fracture detected!

S-C1-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C1-2.text: Our reserve oxygen is blowing into the vacuum! We have less than 48 hours of breathable air in the habitat!

S-C1-2.speaker: Leo
S-C1-2.text: Stay calm, team! Panic consumes more oxygen. Commander, open the deep-space transmitter! We need to demand an emergency high-speed cargo resupply from Earth right now!
Player opens the Earth Logistics Menu and clicks Demand Emergency Oxygen Resupply.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: Emergency transmission received by NASA Kennedy Space Center. Rapid-response Falcon Heavy cargo rocket launched with replacement O₂ pods.

S-C1-2.speaker: MILO
S-C1-2.text: Estimated transit time: 2 Sols. Cabin oxygen reserves are draining.

S-C1-3.text: Player must shed non-vital power, seal interior airlocks, and keep the crew rested to preserve oxygen until the cargo lander thumps down outside.

S-C1-3.speaker: Amir
S-C1-3.text: Cargo lander has touched down! I'm suiting up to haul the new oxygen tanks into the airlock!
Amir replaces the tank. The oxygen gauge surges back to 100%.

S-C1-3.speaker: Leo
S-C1-3.text: Air pressure restored. That was too close, Commander. If that rocket had been delayed by half a day, we wouldn't have survived.

S-C2-1.speaker: MILO
S-C2-1.text: Warning: Orbital sun angle declining. A massive mountain ridge will cast a total shadow over the base for 48 consecutive hours.

S-C2-1.speaker: Amir
S-C2-1.text: Without direct sunlight, our solar panels won't produce a single watt. Outside temperature will plummet to −180 °C.

S-C2-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-1.text: If our electric heaters shut down, the habitat interior will drop below freezing in two hours. Human blood cannot circulate in extreme cold. The crew will freeze to death.

S-C2-1.speaker: Leo
S-C2-1.text: Commander, build high-capacity battery banks immediately. We must store every joule of excess solar power before the shadow arrives.
Player builds Battery Banks and toggles off research labs and floodlights.

S-C2-2.text: Total darkness falls across the base. The base switches to battery power.

S-C2-2.speaker: MILO
S-C2-2.text: Solar generation: 0.0 kW. Battery discharge active.

S-C2-2.speaker: Amir
S-C2-2.text: Captain! The exterior cooling lines on Battery Bank 2 are freezing solid! The battery can't release power when frozen!

S-C2-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-2.text: Cabin temperature is falling fast: 18 °C... 12 °C... 6 °C! We're shivering uncontrollably!

S-C2-2.speaker: Leo
S-C2-2.text: Amir, reroute emergency heating loops to the battery core! Commander, switch auxiliary power to the thermal grid!
Player reroutes the circuit on the thermal panel. Warm coolant pulses through the battery casing.

S-C2-2.speaker: Amir
S-C2-2.text: Coolant thawed! Power is surging through the main bus! Heaters are back online!

S-C2-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C2-2.text: Cabin temperature stabilizing at 21 °C. Good thinking, Commander.

S-C3-1.speaker: Nia
S-C3-1.text: Commander! NASA DONKI has detected a Category X solar flare on the Sun's surface at sunspot 4109.

S-C3-1.speaker: MILO
S-C3-1.text: A Coronal Mass Ejection is traveling directly along the Earth-Moon line. High-energy proton shockwave will hit our coordinates in approximately 90 minutes.

S-C3-1.speaker: Leo
S-C3-1.text: Our inflatable habitat walls are thin aluminum and Kevlar. They won't stop cosmic protons. We need heavy shielding.

S-C3-1.speaker: Nia
S-C3-1.text: We need two layers: pile lunar regolith over the roof using the automated scooper, and retreat into the underground storm vault surrounded by our water tanks.
Player builds Regolith Shielding and moves crew to the Underground Storm Vault.

S-C3-2.text: The radiation storm strikes. Exterior sensors read off the charts.

S-C3-2.speaker: MILO
S-C3-2.text: Exterior radiation levels spiking: 140 mSv/h. Outside exposure would cause fatal acute radiation poisoning within 15 minutes.

S-C3-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C3-2.text: The water tanks and lunar soil are absorbing the particles. Interior dosimeter reads safe.

S-C3-2.speaker: Amir
S-C3-2.text: Hear that static on the radio? The Sun is throwing everything it's got at us. But we're safe underground.

S-C3-2.speaker: Leo
S-C3-2.text: The Moon gave us the weapon to defend ourselves: its own soil. Outstanding preparation, Commander.

S-C4-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C4-1.text: Inventory count is complete. Our packaged rations from Earth are down to their last week. If we don't start producing food here, we'll have to abandon the mission.

S-C4-1.speaker: Nia
S-C4-1.text: We're not going anywhere. Inside Shackleton's shadow, there's ancient water ice. If we drill into the permafrost, we can melt it and run our hydroponics.
Player builds Water Extractor and runs power down into the crater.

S-C4-1.speaker: MILO
S-C4-1.text: Water extraction online: +10 L/h of purified water flowing into reservoir tanks.

S-C4-2.text: Hydroponic growth lights turn magenta. Seed trays are slotted into nutrient pipes.

S-C4-2.speaker: Nia
S-C4-2.text: Greenhouse trays deployed: lettuce, radishes, and dwarf wheat. The plants absorb our exhaled carbon dioxide and release fresh oxygen while feeding us.

S-C4-2.speaker: Amir
S-C4-2.text: Look at those tiny green sprouts! First time fresh living plants have grown in lunar regolith.

S-C4-2.speaker: Leo
S-C4-2.text: From this day on, we aren't visitors surviving on canned food from Earth. We are inhabitants of the Moon.

S-C5-1.text: The ground shudders violently. Dust erupts from the crater walls. A loud CRACK echoes through the structure.

S-C5-1.speaker: MILO
S-C5-1.text: CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Moonquake detected, Magnitude 5.2! Power distribution bus severed! Habitat pressure dropping rapidly: 70 kPa... 60 kPa!

S-C5-1.speaker: Daniel
S-C5-1.text: Captain Leo was outside performing exterior maintenance! His suit telemetry says he's trapped at the primary airlock exterior valve!

S-C5-1.speaker: Leo
S-C5-1.text: Comms... cracking... valve jammed by seismic dust... suit oxygen... at 8%... cannot reach the manual override...

S-C5-1.speaker: Amir
S-C5-1.text: His suit oxygen is almost gone! He has about 60 seconds before he suffocates!

S-C5-2.text: Toggles emergency batteries directly to the airlock power bus.
Cleans the solar panels using automated electrostatic pulse.
Reroutes the backup power cable to the primary life-support loop.
The airlock hisses loudly. Pressure equalizes. Inner doors swing open. Daniel and Amir drag Leo inside.

S-C5-2.speaker: Daniel
S-C5-2.text: Pulse is strong! He's breathing! Get his helmet off!

S-C5-2.speaker: Leo
S-C5-2.text: Coughing... That... was closer than I like, team.

S-C5-2.speaker: Leo
S-C5-2.text: Commander... when every alarm in the base was screaming at once, you didn't freeze. You made the hard calls, you prioritized the right systems, and you brought me home.

S-C5-2.speaker: Leo
S-C5-2.text: I couldn't have asked for a better officer at the console.

S-EPI-1.text: The habitat glows softly in the permanent light of the crater rim. Earth hangs in the velvet black sky like a bright jewel.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: Commander, when we landed, Shackleton Crater was an empty, frozen desert ready to swallow us whole.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: You managed our power, you never let our oxygen run out, you called for help when we needed it, and you kept us alive when disaster struck.

S-EPI-1.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-1.text: You aren't just a student anymore. You are a true Mission Commander.
A golden NASA achievement certificate appears on screen.

S-EPI-2.text: M.I.L.O.'s terminal beeps with an encrypted transmission from NASA Deep Space Logistics.

S-EPI-2.speaker: MILO
S-EPI-2.text: Commander, high-priority transmission incoming from Earth.

S-EPI-2.speaker: MILO
S-EPI-2.text: It concerns a new expedition. Target destination: Mars. Distance: 225 million kilometers.
The screen shifts from the silver Moon to a rotating red globe: MARS.

S-EPI-2.speaker: Amir
S-EPI-2.text: Mars? That's going to take a lot of oxygen tanks!

S-EPI-2.speaker: Nia
S-EPI-2.text: Real soil, ancient riverbeds, towering volcanoes... think of the science!

S-EPI-2.speaker: Leo
S-EPI-2.text: Enjoy this victory, Commander. You earned it. But keep your spacesuit ready... Mars is waiting for us.
